text:
Brown Elementary had 18 multiracial students in 2024-25
K. B. Beebe
Eighteen students at Brown Elementary School were identified as multiracial in the 2024-25 school year, a 20% increase from the previous year, according to the Michigan Department of Education.
School records show Brown Elementary enrolled 434 students in the 2024-25 school year. Multiracial students accounted for 4.1% of the student body, the third-largest ethnic group. White students were the largest group, making up 84.8% (368) of enrollment.
The school is in Huron School District, which has its central office in New Boston.
Of the five schools in Huron School District, Huron High School had the largest enrollment of multiracial students in the 2024-25 school year.
Academic performance in Michigan remains below pre-pandemic levels. The 2024 NAEP results show the share of students reaching the basic benchmark in core subjects is about 10 percentage points lower than in 2019—except for fourth-grade math, which fell by just 2 points.
Achievement gaps between ethnic groups persist. On average, Hispanic students scored 15 points below white students. The gap was wider for Black students, who scored about 30 points lower than their white peers.
